architecture.mechanism: Sulfonate detergent polar groups intercalate between sludge particles with hydrophobic tails extending into the oil phase, preventing colloidal aggregation that forms piston deposits.
architecture.intervention: Formulate the engine oil with an optimized sulfonate-based detergent package whose polar-group/tail architecture is tuned to keep insoluble sludge particles dispersed in the base oil matrix, preserving ring-pack and cylinder-wall cleanliness.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced piston deposit and sludge accumulation on critical friction surfaces, less ring sticking and surface roughening, lower friction and waste-heat losses, and recovery of thermodynamic efficiency while remaining a practical, emissions-compliant automotive engine.
architecture.falsification_test: Run a dynamometer piston-cleansliness/oxidation test with and without the optimized sulfonate package, measuring piston deposit mass, ring-pack friction torque, blow-by, drain-oil particle size distribution, and fuel consumption; the mechanism is falsified if intercalation is confirmed (particle size stays small) yet deposit mass, friction torque, and efficiency do not improve.
